stories.title: Critical FortiMail Zero-Day Flaw Exploited in Attacks Allows Unauthenticated Arbitrary File Writes
stories.abstract: Fortinet has patched a critical path traversal vulnerability, CVE-2026-104286, affecting multiple FortiMail versions. The flaw allows unauthenticated attackers to perform arbitrary file writes. CISA has confirmed active exploitation and added the vulnerability to its Known Exploited Vulnerabilities catalog.
stories.why: This critical vulnerability allows remote code execution or system compromise, and active exploitation is already occurring in the wild.
stories.action: Update FortiMail to version 8.0.2, 7.6.7, 7.4.9, or migrate to the 7.4 branch immediately.

stories.title: CISA Adds Exploited Cisco Catalyst SD-WAN Manager Auth Bypass to KEV
stories.abstract: CISA has updated its Known Exploited Vulnerabilities catalog to include five actively exploited flaws affecting Zammad, Fortinet, and Cisco products. These vulnerabilities allow for session fixation, privilege escalation, path traversal, and remote authentication bypass on exposed systems.
stories.why: Active exploitation of these vulnerabilities indicates they are currently being weaponized by threat actors to gain unauthorized access or control over enterprise infrastructure.
stories.action: Review your environment for Zammad, FortiMail, and Cisco Catalyst SD-WAN Manager and apply available security patches immediately.

stories.title: Apple CoreGraphics PoC Emerges as WhatsApp PDF Checks Hint at Possible Delivery Path
stories.abstract: A proof-of-concept exploit has surfaced for CVE-2026-86950, a critical out-of-bounds write vulnerability in Apple's CoreGraphics engine. Attackers are leveraging malicious PDF files with malformed fonts to target specific users, potentially enabling remote code execution on unpatched iPhones and Mac devices.
stories.why: This zero-day is actively exploited in the wild, posing a significant risk for targeted surveillance and remote compromise of Apple hardware.
stories.action: Update all iOS, iPadOS, and macOS devices to the latest available security versions immediately.

stories.title: Armatura LLC Armatura One
stories.abstract: Armatura One access control software contains multiple critical vulnerabilities, including deserialization flaws and hard-coded credentials. Exploitation allows attackers to execute arbitrary code with root privileges, compromise databases, or seize control of physical security infrastructure.
stories.why: These flaws enable full system takeover and physical security bypass, posing severe risks to critical infrastructure environments.
stories.action: Update Armatura One to version 4.7.2 or Armatura One (USA) to 4.6.1 immediately.

stories.title: Warlock Exploits SharePoint Flaws to Disable Security Tools and Deploy Ransomware
stories.abstract: A China-linked threat actor identified as Warlock is actively targeting government, education, and critical infrastructure sectors in Spanish and Portuguese-speaking regions. The group leverages various Microsoft SharePoint vulnerabilities to disable security software and deploy ransomware within compromised environments.
stories.why: The actor's ability to neutralize security tools post-exploitation poses a significant risk to incident response and detection capabilities in critical infrastructure.

stories.title: Cisco security advisory (AV26-978)
stories.abstract: Cisco has disclosed an authentication bypass vulnerability in its Catalyst SD-WAN Manager. The flaw, tracked as CVE-2026-76504, is currently being actively exploited in the wild, leading CISA to add the vulnerability to its Known Exploited Vulnerabilities catalog.
stories.why: Active exploitation of authentication bypass flaws in network management infrastructure poses a critical risk of unauthorized administrative access and system compromise.
stories.action: Update Cisco Catalyst SD-WAN Manager to the latest patched versions immediately.

stories.title: Anthropic's super bug-hunting model Mythos is hardcore good at math, as latest vuln under attack shows
stories.abstract: Anthropic's Mythos model is being utilized to identify and exploit software vulnerabilities. Security researchers have observed active exploitation attempts originating from China-based IP addresses, highlighting the increasing role of advanced AI in automating the discovery and weaponization of security flaws.
stories.why: AI-driven vulnerability research significantly lowers the barrier for attackers to weaponize zero-days, accelerating the threat lifecycle for defenders.

stories.title: Fortra security advisory (AV26-987)
stories.abstract: Fortra released security updates for its BoKS privileged access management software to address multiple critical vulnerabilities. The flaws include heap overflows, stack buffer overflows, and out-of-bounds read issues that could allow attackers to bypass authentication or execute arbitrary shell commands.
stories.why: These vulnerabilities affect core privileged access infrastructure, potentially granting unauthenticated attackers full control over managed systems and sensitive administrative credentials.
stories.action: Update BoKS Manager and Core Privileged Access Manager to versions 8.1.0.30, 9.0.0.7, or 10.1.1.0.

stories.title: Citrix NetScaler CVE-2026-88772 Exploit Details Show Pre-Auth Path to Shellcode Execution
stories.abstract: Citrix has confirmed active exploitation of two critical zero-day vulnerabilities, CVE-2026-88771 and CVE-2026-88772, affecting NetScaler ADC and Gateway appliances. The flaws include a high-severity memory overflow issue within the DTLS protocol implementation, allowing potential unauthorized access or system compromise.
stories.why: These vulnerabilities are being actively exploited in the wild and carry high CVSS scores, posing a significant risk to edge infrastructure security.
stories.action: Apply the latest security patches provided by Citrix immediately.

stories.title: Johnson Controls EasyIO Neo Series EC and CW Controllers
stories.abstract: Johnson Controls has disclosed vulnerabilities in its EasyIO FG, Neo, and FS32 product lines. These flaws, identified as CVE-2026-64892 and CVE-2026-64893, could allow unauthorized actors to intercept sensitive credentials, session data, and other critical system information.
stories.why: These vulnerabilities impact building automation systems used in critical infrastructure, potentially exposing sensitive control network data to remote attackers.
stories.action: Update EasyIO FG, Neo, and FS32 firmware to the latest available versions.

stories.title: Police Arrest 16-Year-Old Suspected of Running KillSec, Seize Ransomware Leak Site and Servers
stories.abstract: International law enforcement dismantled the KillSec ransomware operation, seizing servers and a leak site containing 110 terabytes of exfiltrated data. Authorities arrested three individuals, including a 16-year-old suspected of acting as the group's primary administrator.
stories.why: The takedown highlights the ongoing trend of juvenile involvement in sophisticated cybercrime syndicates and the efficacy of coordinated cross-border police operations.

stories.title: Dell CSM Flaws Enable Unauthenticated Admin Access and Root on Kubernetes Nodes
stories.abstract: Dell patched critical vulnerabilities in its Container Storage Modules for Kubernetes, including a flaw in the gRPC server that allows unauthenticated attackers to gain administrative control and root-level access to underlying nodes.
stories.why: These flaws permit full system compromise of Kubernetes clusters, posing a severe risk to data integrity and infrastructure control.
stories.action: Update Dell Container Storage Modules to the latest patched versions immediately.

stories.title: Attackers Exploit Zimbra Flaw to Deploy Web Shells and Harvest Authentication Secrets
stories.abstract: Attackers are actively exploiting a critical command injection vulnerability in Zimbra Collaboration Suite, identified as CVE-2026-73570. By leveraging the Simple Network Management Protocol, threat actors can achieve remote code execution to install web shells and exfiltrate sensitive mailbox credentials.
stories.why: This flaw allows unauthenticated attackers to gain full system control, posing a severe risk to email confidentiality and infrastructure integrity.
stories.action: Apply the latest security patches for Zimbra Collaboration Suite immediately.

stories.title: Fortinet sounds the alarm over actively exploited FortiMail zero-day
stories.abstract: Fortinet has disclosed a critical zero-day vulnerability in FortiMail that is currently being exploited in the wild. The flaw allows unauthenticated attackers to compromise affected systems, and some administrators are still awaiting the release of necessary security patches.
stories.why: Unauthenticated remote code execution vulnerabilities in edge appliances pose a severe risk of initial access and network compromise.
stories.action: Monitor Fortinet security advisories and apply patches immediately upon release.

stories.title: Kiteworks & Citrix Incidents Show Challenges of Zero-Day Response
stories.abstract: Recent security incidents involving Kiteworks and Citrix highlight significant inconsistencies in how vendors manage zero-day disclosures. Organizations faced varying levels of transparency and remediation guidance, ranging from emergency system shutdowns to delayed public acknowledgments of active exploitation.
stories.why: Inconsistent vendor communication during zero-day events complicates incident response, risk assessment, and the ability for security teams to protect their infrastructure effectively.

stories.title: [Control Systems] Moxa security advisory (AV26-995)
stories.abstract: Moxa has disclosed multiple vulnerabilities affecting its MGate 3000 and 5000 series protocol gateways. Administrators should review the manufacturer's security advisory to determine the impact on their industrial control systems and identify available firmware remediation paths.
stories.why: Unpatched vulnerabilities in industrial gateways can provide attackers with unauthorized access or control over critical operational technology networks.
stories.action: Review Moxa security advisory AV26-995 and apply available firmware updates to affected MGate devices.

stories.title: Antino Backdoor Uses Outlook and OneDrive for C2 in China-Nexus Espionage Campaign
stories.abstract: A China-linked threat actor is targeting government and policy entities across Asia with a novel backdoor called Antino. The malware leverages Microsoft Outlook and OneDrive infrastructure to facilitate command-and-control communications, enabling long-term espionage against organizations in countries including India, Taiwan, and the Philippines.
stories.why: This campaign demonstrates sophisticated abuse of legitimate cloud services for stealthy data exfiltration and persistent remote access in sensitive geopolitical environments.

stories.title: Microsoft’s X account hacked in crypto pump-and-dump scheme
stories.abstract: Unauthorized actors gained control of Microsoft's primary X account to broadcast a cryptocurrency pump-and-dump scheme. The attackers leveraged the company's massive follower base to promote a specific token before the posts were eventually removed.
stories.why: High-profile account takeovers demonstrate that even major organizations remain vulnerable to social engineering or platform-level security failures, threatening brand reputation and user trust.

stories.title: Attackers Abuse ChatGPT Custom GPTs to Deliver RAT via ClickFix Lures
YARA-X 1.21.0 Release, (Sat, Oct 3rd)
stories.abstract: The YARA-X project has released version 1.21.0, which introduces five functional enhancements and addresses four identified software bugs.
stories.why: Security teams relying on YARA-X for malware detection and file analysis should review the changelog to ensure stability and feature compatibility.

stories.title: Warlock ransomware breach SharePoint in water, telecom operator attacks
stories.abstract: A China-aligned threat actor known as Warlock is targeting critical infrastructure, including water utilities and telecommunications providers. The group gains initial network access by exploiting vulnerabilities within Microsoft SharePoint installations to facilitate their ransomware operations.
stories.why: The targeting of essential services and critical infrastructure by state-linked actors indicates a shift toward high-impact, disruptive cyber espionage and extortion.
stories.action: Audit and patch all Microsoft SharePoint instances immediately.

stories.title: MI5 Says China’s MSS Funded Research Involving 100+ U.K.-Linked Academics
stories.abstract: MI5 has issued a formal warning regarding the China General Technology Research Institute, alleging it serves as a front for Chinese state intelligence. Over 100 British academics have reportedly conducted research for the organization, inadvertently supporting Beijing's espionage and data collection operations.
stories.why: This highlights the ongoing risk of academic research being weaponized for foreign intelligence gathering and state-sponsored technology transfer.

stories.title: Frontline Education breach exposes school district employee data
stories.abstract: Frontline Education confirmed a data breach involving unauthorized access to its systems via a third-party software vulnerability. The incident resulted in the exfiltration of sensitive employee information, including Social Security numbers, across various school districts utilizing the platform.
stories.why: Supply chain compromises in educational software platforms create significant downstream risks for sensitive PII and potential identity theft for school district staff.

stories.title: ThreatsDay: AI-Powered Zero-Day Chain, 543K Live Secrets, Model Inspection RCE and 13 More Stories
stories.abstract: Recent security findings highlight how routine system functions like caching, model inspection, and data storage are being weaponized. Attackers are increasingly exploiting these standard operational processes to execute code or gain unauthorized access, proving that mundane features often harbor significant security risks.
stories.why: Standard system features are frequently overlooked during threat modeling, creating blind spots where attackers can execute code or leak sensitive information.

stories.title: Bitget Confirms Third-Party Zero-Day Behind $387.5 Million Cryptocurrency Theft
stories.abstract: Bitget reported that a recent $387.5 million theft was facilitated by a zero-day vulnerability found within third-party security software. Forensic analysis by SlowMist uncovered custom tooling used by the attackers to exploit these external dependencies.
stories.why: Supply chain vulnerabilities in security tooling can bypass perimeter defenses, highlighting the risks of integrating third-party software into critical infrastructure.

stories.title: Danish university DTU breach exposes data of up to 200,000 people
stories.abstract: The Technical University of Denmark suffered a significant data breach after unauthorized actors compromised its identity and access management infrastructure. The incident resulted in the potential exposure of personal information belonging to approximately 200,000 individuals associated with the institution.
stories.why: Identity management systems are high-value targets; their compromise often grants attackers broad access to sensitive user credentials and downstream institutional resources.

stories.title: macOS Users Targeted by Fake Zoom Installer Carrying CloudSyncD Backdoor
stories.abstract: Threat actors are distributing a malicious Zoom installer for macOS that deploys the CloudSyncD backdoor. The malware uses a two-stage execution process to harvest user credentials and establish persistent unauthorized access to compromised systems.
stories.why: This campaign demonstrates sophisticated social engineering targeting common productivity software to bypass macOS security controls and gain administrative persistence.

stories.title: Monta monta.app
stories.abstract: Multiple critical vulnerabilities in the Monta charging management platform expose systems to unauthorized administrative access and denial-of-service attacks. The flaws include improper authentication, session management failures, and credential protection issues, impacting all versions of the application.
stories.why: These flaws allow remote attackers to hijack charging infrastructure, posing significant risks to energy and transportation sectors.
stories.action: Contact the vendor to obtain and apply the necessary security patches for your deployment.

stories.title: ABB Protection and Control IED Manager PCM600
stories.abstract: ABB's PCM600 software contains two vulnerabilities involving improper path restrictions and incorrect permission assignments. These flaws allow local users to escalate privileges or overwrite arbitrary files by exploiting the Scheduler Service, which runs with elevated LocalSystem account permissions.
stories.why: Exploitation could grant unauthorized users administrative control over industrial control system management software, posing significant risks to energy sector infrastructure.
stories.action: Update ABB PCM600 to a version beyond 2.14.

stories.title: Podcast: The FBI Was Hacked. We’ve Seen the Data
stories.abstract: Journalists at 404 Media report obtaining evidence of a significant security breach involving the FBI. The investigation suggests unauthorized access to sensitive bureau data, though specific details regarding the scope and method of the intrusion remain limited.
stories.why: Unauthorized access to federal law enforcement databases poses severe risks to ongoing investigations, informant safety, and national security intelligence.

stories.title: OpenAI Parts Ways With Three Safety Researchers Over Sensitive Information Mishandling
Mississippi mayor says ransomware incident led city to shut down systems
stories.abstract: Vicksburg, Mississippi, suspended municipal digital operations following a ransomware attack. Local officials are currently collaborating with the FBI to investigate the breach and restore affected government services.
stories.why: Municipalities remain high-value targets for ransomware actors, often leading to significant service outages and potential exposure of sensitive constituent data.

stories.title: Meari IoT Cloud Platform OpenAPI Service
stories.abstract: The Meari IoT Cloud Platform OpenAPI Service contains authorization flaws that enable authenticated users to modify device settings, execute unauthorized actions, and exfiltrate sensitive data, including owner information, network details, and device credentials.
stories.why: Broken access control in cloud-based IoT management platforms can lead to widespread device hijacking and unauthorized access to sensitive user and network data.
